h1: The 6 Best Cordless Phones With Intercoms of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Intercom Cordless Phones: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six cordless phones with handset-to-handset intercom, compared on handset count, range, Bluetooth and call blocking.
summary: The Panasonic KX-TGD864W is our best intercom cordless phone, with four handsets, Link2Cell Bluetooth and a voice assistant. The VTech IS8151-5 is the choice for big properties, with five handsets and a 2300 ft range. The AT&T BL102-4 and DL72319 cover mid-sized homes, and the VTech VG232-2 is the cheap two-handset option.
intro: An intercom only earns its place if there are enough handsets to talk between, and that is where most buyers misjudge. Two handsets give you one conversation path, while four or five let you page a whole household from the kitchen. The catch is that handset count drives the price faster than any other feature, so the right pick depends on how many rooms you really want to reach.

We reviewed six systems on paper, comparing handset count, listed range, Bluetooth and cell linking, call blocking and answering features. Every model here lists an intercom, so the ranking turns on how much else each one adds around it.

products.name: Panasonic Cordless Phone with Answering Machine, Link2Cell Bluetooth Home Phones, Voice Assistant and Advanced Call Blocking, Expandable System with 4 Handsets, Cordless Telephone - KX-TGD864W
products.verdict: Four handsets plus Bluetooth, a voice assistant and call blocking.
products.description:
The KX-TGD864W comes with four handsets, Link2Cell Bluetooth, a voice assistant and advanced call blocking. The system is expandable, and there is an answering machine in the base.

It takes the top spot because it stacks the most useful extras on top of a four-handset intercom, which the VTech VG232-4 only matches on handset count. The tradeoff is cost, because it lands among the priciest sets here at $100 to $200.

Pick it for a family home where cell calls and voice features matter. Skip it if you only need to buzz between two rooms.
cons: More than a small home needs
products.idealFor: Family homes that want intercom plus cell linking.

products.name: VTech IS8151-5 Super Long Range 5 Handset DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone for Home with Answering Machine, 2300 ft Range, Call Blocking, Bluetooth, Headset Jack, Power Backup, Intercom, Expandable to 12 HS
products.verdict: Five handsets, 2300 ft range and power backup.
products.description:
The IS8151-5 lists five handsets, a 2300 ft range, call blocking, Bluetooth, a headset jack and power backup. It expands to 12 handsets and includes an answering machine.

It ranks second because the five-handset reach and power backup suit big properties better than the Panasonic, which has no stated range or backup. The price is in the same $100 to $200 range.

Buy it for a large home, workshop or farm with outbuildings. Skip it for an apartment, where the range is wasted.

products.name: AT&T BL102-4 DECT 6.0 4-Handset Cordless Phone for Home with Answering Machine, Call Blocking, Caller ID Announcer, Audio Assist, Intercom, and Unsurpassed Range
products.verdict: Four handsets with call blocking and caller ID announcer.
products.description:
The BL102-4 supplies four handsets, an answering machine, call blocking, a caller ID announcer and audio assist alongside the intercom.

It ranks third because it has no Bluetooth or voice assistant, which the Panasonic adds. It makes up for that with a clearer focus on core call handling, and the price is in the $100 to $200 bucket.

Buy it for a larger home that wants blocking and an announcer. Skip it if you want cell linking.
products.idealFor: Larger homes focused on core calling.

products.award: Best Cell Link on a Budget
products.name: AT&T DL72319 DECT 6.0 3-Handset Cordless Phone for Home with Connect to Cell, Call Blocking, 1.8" Backlit Screen, Big Buttons, Intercom, and Unsurpassed Range
products.verdict: Connect to Cell with three handsets for less.
products.description:
Three handsets come in the DL72319 box, and the feature list covers cell pairing through Connect to Cell, spam filtering, large keys and the intercom, all behind a small 1.8 inch lit screen.

It ranks fourth because three handsets cover a mid-sized home while the AT&T BL102-4 has one more, and it lacks an answering machine in the listing. It sits in the $50 to $100 bucket, below the four-handset models.

Buy it for a mid-sized home that wants to pull cell calls onto the handsets. Skip it if you want voicemail.
products.idealFor: Mid-sized homes that take cell calls at home.
products.skipIf: You rely on an answering machine.

products.name: VTech Cordless Phone with 4 Handsets, Big Buttons, Large Backlit Display, Answering Machine, DECT 6.0, Whole-Home Coverage, Intercom, Easy to Use - VG232-4
products.verdict: Four easy-to-read handsets and whole-home coverage.
products.description:
The VG232-4 has four handsets, big buttons, a large backlit display, an answering machine and whole-home coverage.

It ranks fifth because it skips Bluetooth and call blocking in its listing, which the Panasonic and AT&T four-handset kits both offer. It is the easiest to read and sits in the $50 to $100 bucket.

Buy it for a household with older users who need large buttons. Skip it if spam calls are a problem.

products.name: VTech Cordless Phone with 2 Handsets, Big Buttons, Large Backlit Display, Answering Machine, DECT 6.0, Caller ID, Intercom, Easy to Use, Silver/Black - VG232-2
products.verdict: The simplest way to get an intercom between two rooms.
products.description:
The VG232-2 ships with two handsets, big buttons, a large backlit display, an answering machine, caller ID and intercom.

It ranks last because two handsets are the minimum an intercom needs and it lacks the call blocking of the AT&T kits. The lowest cost in the guide, in the $50 to $100 bucket, is the draw.

Buy it for a small home where you only need to page between two rooms. Skip it if you want to add more handsets later without checking compatibility.
products.idealFor: Small homes paging between two rooms.
products.skipIf: You need more than two handsets.

whatMatters.detail: An intercom connects handsets, so the count decides how many rooms you reach. Two handsets give one path, while four or five let you page a household. Check the number in the title.
Range is how far a handset can roam from the base before it drops out. Walls reduce it, so open-air figures overstate real use. Look for a feet figure in the title.
Link2Cell and Connect to Cell pair a mobile with the base so cell calls ring on home handsets. This helps where cell signal is poor. Look for these exact names.
Most cordless bases die in a power cut. Power backup keeps at least one handset alive. Check for the phrase in the listing.
Blocking stops flagged numbers from ringing through. It matters for homes that get frequent spam. Look for 'call blocking' or 'advanced call block'.

faq.q: How does a cordless phone intercom work?
faq.a: It lets one handset call another through the base without using the phone line. You select the handset and speak.
Many systems are expandable, such as the IS8151-5 up to 12 handsets. Always buy matching handsets compatible with your base.
Only if you take cell calls at home or have weak signal. Otherwise it adds cost.

faq.q: How do I use the intercom?
faq.a: Press the intercom key on one handset and choose another. Some systems also page all handsets at once.

faq.q: How far will the intercom reach?
faq.a: It depends on walls and floors. The IS8151-5 lists 2300 ft in open air, but expect less indoors.

faq.q: Do these phones work during a power cut?
faq.a: Most do not. The VTech IS8151-5 lists power backup, so it is the one to consider.

finalTake: The Panasonic KX-TGD864W is the best cordless phone with intercom for most families, thanks to four handsets and Bluetooth. Pick the VTech IS8151-5 for a large property. The AT&T BL102-4 is the value four-handset option, and the VG232-2 covers a two-room home cheaply.
